text:
Nina: Observability flagged apiserver FD exhaustion during a large GPU onboarding window in us-west2 at ~03:40 UTC. apiserver started returning 5xx and controller-manager lost leader lease.
Omar: Interesting — not seeing conntrack or SNAT exhaustion this time. Any new monitoring agents or DaemonSets rolled out?
Nina: We pushed a new per-node profiler daemonset that opens a long-lived watch per pod to stream metrics. It joined with the GPU nodes at the same time.
SRE-Oncall: grabbing apiserver logs. snippet: 
```
E0311 03:40:12.451 server.go:645] http: Accept error: accept tcp 0.0.0.0:6443: accept4: too many open files
E0311 03:40:12.452 server.go:651] REST request failed: Post https://etcd-usw2:2379/kv: dial tcp 10.9.3.12:2379: i/o timeout
```
MetricsBot: [metric] apiserver: file_descriptors_in_use = 3276, fd_limit = 4096 at 03:40:13
Omar: If the profiler creates one watch per pod and we scale +1000 pods across GPUs, that's a lot of fds. apiserver uses a fd per accepted connection + file handles under load.
Nina: controller-manager log: 
```
W0311 03:40:14 controller_utils.go:456] lost leader lease: context deadline exceeded
I0311 03:40:15 manager.go:312] Shutting down due to lost leader election
```
SRE-Oncall: Quick triage steps in play: 1) roll back the profiler DaemonSet to the previous image, 2) increase apiserver systemd LimitNOFILE to 262144 as emergency, 3) cordon high-churn GPU nodes.
Karen: Rolled back profiler on the GPU node pool at 03:41. systemd patch for kube-apiserver applied to control plane VMs.
Omar: We should also evaluate moving to multiplexed streams (aggregated watch proxy) instead of per-pod watches. That reduces fds drastically.
Nina: Agreed. Also consider enabling watch throttle/rate limits on the profiler and limit watch lifetime.
SRE-Oncall: After rollback, FD usage dropped: apiserver file_descriptors_in_use = 980 at 03:43 and 5xxs dropped. Controller-manager reacquired leader after ~2m.
Karen: Action items: document the profiler rollout policy, add a preflight check for expected FD growth when DaemonSets scale, add apiserver fd headroom alert, and evaluate shared metric scraper architecture.
Omar: Cost tradeoff note: moving to a dedicated scrape-tier (extra small pods) vs increasing apiserver limits — extra scraper pods add CPU but avoid inflated apiserver surface area. Finance wants a rough monthly cost for both options.
Nina: I'll open a ticket with the cost estimates and a proposal for an aggregated watch proxy.
SRE-Oncall: Adding a dashboard panel for fd_headroom and a canary gating rule for high-fanout DaemonSets.
Karen: Let's also add a runbook step: check for new DaemonSets that create watches before approving large GPU scale-ups.
Nina: Thanks team — marking stable once controller-manager has held leader for 30m. :white_check_mark:
